title: A Orbit for the Echo
premise: Astrid Vasquez has spent twelve years smuggling memories through the contested orbits of Halcyon Station, keeping his head down and his past buried. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream of a burning habitat, Astrid recognizes the imagery as a memory he once smuggled and erased from himself. Digging in, he uncovers evidence that the Meridian Massacre—officially a reactor accident that never killed anyone—was real, and that the station's ruling consortium rewrote every record, including the minds of witnesses. As the jump window to the inner system closes, Astrid must choose between the loyalty he owes the crew who sheltered him and the truth owed to the massacre's orphaned survivors; in the end he broadcasts the children's shared dream across every public screen, sacrificing his ship and freedom so the dead are remembered before the window seals.
about_author: Wren Okafor is a former maritime radio operator who grew up between Lagos and a research vessel in the South Atlantic, where stories were the only cargo that never got taxed. Their fiction explores what people carry when they can no longer trust their own recollections of home.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A routine customs run through Halcyon's checkpoint goes wrong when a hidden memory shard nearly triggers a scan alert. We learn his trade, his forged identity, and his rule: never ask what's inside the cargo. Emotional beat: controlled paranoia masking deep loneliness.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Alike
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Imani, a nine-year-old whose dream of a burning corridor is identical to forty other children's dreams. Her teacher reports it; officials dismiss it as a viral rumor. Beat: eerie innocence colliding with institutional denial.

chapters.title: Twelve Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He hears about the shared dream at his regular dive bar and feels cold recognition—the burning corridor matches a memory he erased from his own mind years ago. Beat: dread surfacing through practiced numbness.

chapters.title: The Client with No Face
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. An anonymous client offers triple rates to smuggle a sealed archive out on the next jump window—and warns him to forget the children's dream. The threat confirms someone powerful cares. Beat: temptation sharpened by fear.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. She draws the dream: a habitat ring, a door marked MERIDIAN-7, figures in vacuum suits who don't help. Her grandmother goes pale and burns the drawing. Beat: the first adult complicity revealed.

chapters.title: Ghost in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He bribes a records clerk and finds Meridian-7 listed as 'decommissioned, zero casualties'—but the decommission date postdates the fire in the dream. Someone edited history badly. Beat: the thrill and terror of a crack in the official story.

chapters.title: Crew of the Long Silence
chapters.summary: POV of Dez, Astrid's smuggler mentor and captain figure, who begs him to drop it: 'You want to know why you're invisible? Because we made you that way.' Beat: loyalty weaponized against truth.

chapters.title: What Was Taken From Me
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Under a black-market mnemonic probe, Astrid recovers fragments: he was on Meridian-7 as a child. His entire identity may be a reconstruction. Beat: shattering self-recognition—he is both smuggler and contraband.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV of Director Sefa Oyelaran, consortium security chief, who authorized the memory wipes as 'mercy' after the massacre and now must decide whether Astrid is a loose end or an asset. Beat: chillingly humane villainy.

chapters.title: Orphans of a Nonexistent Fire
chapters.summary: Astrid and Imani meet; her dream contains details only a survivor would know—including his mother's voice singing in Edo. Beat: grief arriving sideways, through a child.

chapters.title: Smuggling the Truth
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He plans to move the recovered archive like cargo: split into shards, hidden in ordinary memory-stones, run past customs one piece at a time. Beat: purpose replacing fear; craft as resistance.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Dock Nine
chapters.summary: Dez sells Astrid's route to the consortium to protect the crew. Two couriers are arrested; one shard is seized. Beat: loyalty's cost made literal, and Astrid's rage at being protected into silence again.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Sefa offers Astrid amnesty and a clean new identity if he surrenders the archive—proving she knows exactly what he is. He stalls, buying time. Beat: seduction of forgetting versus the ache of remembering.

chapters.title: The Witness in Cryo
chapters.summary: Imani's POV leads Astrid to a cryo bay holding a massacre survivor kept frozen for twelve years—Sefa's own sister, preserved as blackmail insurance by a rival director. Beat: hope rekindled through an enemy's sin.

chapters.title: Thawing
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Waking the witness risks killing her and exposes them all. In her brief lucidity she names the order-giver: not Sefa, but the consortium's beloved founder. Beat: moral vertigo—the monster is the myth.

chapters.title: Window Closing
chapters.summary: Dez, guilt-ridden, returns with the stolen shard and the crew's tacit blessing—but the jump window leaves in thirty hours and customs is locked down. Beat: reconciliation without absolution.

chapters.title: Every Screen on Halcyon
chapters.summary: Astrid's plan: instead of smuggling the truth out, broadcast it in—piggybacking the children's shared dream onto the station's entertainment grid during the founder's memorial broadcast. Beat: audacity born of desperation.

chapters.title: The Founder's Memorial
chapters.summary: Multi-POV climax. As thousands watch, the dream floods every screen: the fire, the door, the suits that walked away. Sefa chooses at the last second not to jam the signal. Beat: catharsis—a whole station forced to remember at once.

chapters.title: What the Crowd Did Next
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Panic, then gathering: families of the erased converge on Meridian-7's sealed ring and break it open, finding remains and keepsakes. Beat: collective grief becoming collective claim.

chapters.title: The Price of the Broadcast
chapters.summary: Astrid surrenders to spare the crew reprisal; his ship is impounded and his smuggled identity dissolved. Sefa testifies in exchange for prosecuting the founder's faction. Beat: sacrifice accepted without heroics.

chapters.title: Departures
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. The jump window opens; the crew leaves as promised, but leaves Astrid's share and a message: the route stays open. Beat: bittersweet severance—loyalty outlasting presence.

chapters.title: An Orbit for the Echo
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, months later. Working openly as the massacre's archivist, he helps survivors rebuild records from recovered memories. Imani asks if the dreams will stop; he says they're not dreams anymore—they're history. Final beat: identity reclaimed, truth given a permanent orbit.
